episode_title: EP#94: What VCs Say When Founders Aren’t in the Room. Eric Newcomer

real_qa.q: How did Eric Newcomer transition from Bloomberg to building an independent media business on Substack?
real_qa.r: After six years at Bloomberg, Newcomer felt he was doing the same thing and wanted something riskier without moving to another publication. He saw Substack as an exciting newsletter publishing platform focused on subscriptions, which aligned with what he had observed at The Information and Bloomberg's terminal business model. He quit, announced his Substack, and it performed well early on as one of the top 10 tech Substacks, especially during the pandemic when people were seeking digital connection.

real_qa.q: What is the Cerebral Valley AI Summit and when was it first held?
real_qa.r: The Cerebral Valley AI Summit is an annual conference founded by Eric Newcomer focused on AI and venture capital. He hosted the first Cerebral Valley in 2023 right after ChatGPT came out, and the event has grown to become a high-caliber gathering of prominent investors and founders. The conference is designed around getting deserving speakers to participate and creating valuable connections among attendees.

real_qa.q: What is the VC Sentiment Report that Newcomer produces and who does it include?
real_qa.r: Newcomer recently rolled out an anonymous VC Sentiment Report where they interview venture capitalists including current and former members of the Midas List as well as partners running their own firms. The report asks them for their honest take on how close the market is to a bubble, how far away it is, and what companies they are excited about right now.
real_qa.requete: VC Sentiment Report Newcomer venture capitalists

real_qa.q: Why does Newcomer prioritize transparent bias and direct perspective over false objectivity in reporting?
real_qa.r: Newcomer believes people hate non-transparent bias more than they hate bias itself. When launching Newcomer, he said readers would hear his opinion and facts together, making it easy for audiences to understand his perspective and decide whether they agree. He distinguishes this from feature-style magazine reporting that sneaks bias in through selective quotes and framing, instead stating directly: 'you understand that first and foremost, we're trying to get you great facts and information about what's happening. And then when we have our opinion that we can't keep to ourselves, we will say it directly.'

real_qa.q: How does Eric Newcomer use reporting and sourcing to make predictions about venture capital trends?
real_qa.r: Newcomer relies heavily on reporting and talking to people smarter than him who are plugged into the industry. He leaned into this approach by creating the VC Sentiment Report to anonymously interview venture capitalists and understand where their heads are at regarding market conditions and deal flow, allowing him to provide informed takes when people ask him about industry developments.

guest.bio_context: Eric Newcomer started as a journalist in fourth grade as an elementary school newscast anchor and continued through internships at major publications including the New York Times, Macon Telegraph, Sun Sentinel, and Tampa Bay Times. He was the first employee at The Information when Jessica Lessin founded it in 2009, worked at Bloomberg for six years covering technology and venture capital, and in 2021 launched his independent Substack newsletter Newcomer which grew to over 100,000 subscribers. He founded the Cerebral Valley AI Summit conference in 2023 following the ChatGPT release and continues to run both his media business and the annual conference.
